_README: Employer careers endpoints. Public, non-personal, and identical for everyone who looks them up --
which makes this the one file in this repository a stranger can contribute to with no privacy risk.
An entry here says only that somebody verified this employer's board is machine-readable. It is NOT
a watchlist, a recommendation, or a record of anyone's applications. Add employers freely.
careers_url is ALWAYS the company's own page -- stripe.com/careers/search, never
boards.greenhouse.io/stripe. It is the human link, it is what a person actually pastes, and it is
the recovery key: when an employer switches ATS the endpoint dies and the careers page does not, so
that URL is how the new endpoint gets found. The ATS address belongs in params.
Adding one: put the careers page in front of the agent and ask it to find the endpoint. Set
last_verified to the day you checked and verified_returned to what came back. An entry with a stale
date is a guess, and an endpoint that has quietly started returning nothing looks exactly like a
quiet week -- which is the failure this file has to avoid being the cause of.
Seeded 2026-08-25. Every entry was verified by calling it -- and one was wrong anyway.
canary is a requisition id that must appear in the list response. It is how an entry is checked
on a platform that fails open. A canary can go stale when the job is filled -- registry_check.py
reports that as something to look at, not as a failure, because it cannot tell a wrong endpoint
from a closed vacancy and should not pretend to.
VERIFY BY KNOWN-JOB PRESENCE, NOT BY STATUS CODE OR COUNT. Oracle returns 200 and a plausible
number for a siteNumber that does not exist. The Grant Thornton entry was seeded from a 200 and a
count of 152, and was pointing at the wrong site: the right one returns 55 and is the only one
containing their experienced-hires postings. A check that cannot fail is not a check.

params._map_note: loc is all_locations, NOT location_name. location_name carries only the first of thirty countries -- 'Israel' -- so mapping it would drop every Deel role on a location filter for a user eligible for all of them, and say nothing about it

employers.notes: Ashby underneath -- every row carries an ashby_id -- but the public Ashby board returns empty, so this must target deel.com. Publishes a salary band on every role, which is rare and takes PAY out of TBC before any call

employers.canary_note: Data & AI Internal Product Team, Associate Director. If this disappears the job may simply have closed -- re-pick one before assuming the entry is broken
employers.notes: The tenant is an opaque code, not a company name -- it has to be read off their careers URL. CORRECTED 2026-08-25: this was first seeded as CX_1, which returns 152 jobs and does NOT contain their experienced-hires postings. See the fails-open warning under _endpoints.oracle

employers.canary_note: Lead Technical Program Manager, Dublin. Re-pick if it closes
employers.notes: Oracle hosts vary: some are <tenant>.fa.<region>.oraclecloud.com, this one has no region segment. Take the host from the employer's own apply link rather than assuming a pattern

Shared host style: wd<N>.myworkdaysite.com/recruiting/<tenant>/<site>. An adapter that derives the host from the tenant misses every employer on this style, which is why host, tenant and site are three fields and not one

employers.canary_note: No canary needed: Workday 404s on a wrong site, so a 200 is already proof the identifier is right

_endpoints._comment: How to call each ats. Kept here so an adapter and a human read the same thing.

workday.note: The detail call carries the requisition id, the real posting date and the additional locations the listing hides
workday.fails_closed: Unlike Oracle, Workday 404s on a wrong site with an explicit Job_Posting_Site_ID message. A 200 here is real evidence

oracle.note: The quotes around the finder values are required. Without them it returns 400
oracle.WARNING_FAILS_OPEN: An unrecognised siteNumber does NOT error. It returns 200 with the tenant's UNFILTERED job list, which looks like a plausible answer. Grant Thornton returns 152 for CX_1, 55 for CX_1001 and 258 for any nonsense value -- and the 55 is the one that actually contains their experienced-hires postings. NEVER verify an Oracle entry by status code or job count. Verify by checking a known requisition id is present in the response.
